purpose: Compare a simple scene-aware individual-channel pruning score with random, weight and average-ablation rules

score_calibration.selection: Sort eligible training scene names, shuffle with Python Random(42), take 32; from each sorted scene sample evenly spaced indices. Equal weight per selected scene. Only training data contributes.

score_formula: For each channel and calibration scene, delta = ablated mean-image masked MAE minus baseline mean-image masked MAE; average score is mean(delta); scene-aware score is mean(delta)+0.5*max(delta). Rank ascending; break ties by channel index. No clipping of negative deltas.

pruning.random_selection: random.Random(seed).sample(range(200), 8); independent initial random mask per seed

training.loss: mean of per-image MAE over finite positive target pixels

comparison: Evaluate original untrained, original trained for each seed, fixed weight/average/scene candidates before recovery, each trained candidate for each seed, and random candidates before and after recovery. Tune only on all 445 tuning images; summarize pooled, mean-image and per-scene RMSE and delta1. Report paired seeds and all outcomes; no best-seed cherry-picking.
timing: Measure representative candidates and original on desktop TensorRT FP16 after matching output accuracy, preserving raw timings; not Orin or end-to-end. Target hardware still required for hardware-aware claim.
limitations: Novelty is unverified; tuning data already inspected and checkpoint pretraining may overlap NYU training shards. Only one epoch and one proposed lambda; calibration scene sampling is not representative and individual ablations ignore interactions.
